newsitem.title: UK: Stg vaults old ERM floor to 4-1/2-yr high vs mark.
newsitem.headline: Stg vaults old ERM floor to 4-1/2-yr high vs mark.

text.p: Sterling rallied against the mark on Monday, rising above its old floor in the European exchange rate mechanism (ERM) for the first time since the UK abandoned membership of the system in September 1992.
Sterling has risen more than 22 percent against the mark since last August as robust UK economic activity has pointed to higher UK interest rates as the German economy struggled.
Today the pound took advantage of a renewed bout dollar strength against the mark, which suffered across the board from fresh optimism about a timely start to European monetary union.

"The sterling move today has been almost entirely driven by the dollar, with the market bulled up once again about attractive yields in the U.S. and the net effects of EMU," said Peter Von Maydell, senior currency economist at UBS.
The degree to which the U.S. currency was the catalyst for today's move was illustrated by sterling losses against the dollar during the day.
Sterling tends to track the dollar against other European currencies because the UK economic and interest rate cycle is much closer to that in the U.S. than it is to its European neighbours.

Some traders, however, said sterling gains were aided by a Sunday newspaper report which highlighted the fact that U.K. economic data is understating activity and this may necessitate steeper interest rate rises than currently expected. "The fundamental economic and interest rate story behind the higher dollar is still in place and that goes for the pound too," said Peter Wood, currency trader at Bank of Boston.

"Obviously we won't get any rate rises here before the (May 1) election but the market will be betting on one very shortly after when (Bank of England governor Eddie) George holds his first meeting with (Labour finance spokesman) Gordon Brown."
At 1500 GMT, the pound was trading at 2.7870/80 marks, up more than three pfennigs from 2.7533/43 late Friday. Against the dollar, the pound was at $1.6290/00 compared with $1.6370/80 late Friday.

Traders said an array of stop-loss orders for sterling were triggered on a break of the old ERM floor at 2.7780. The psychologically-important 2.80 is now expected to be targetted by dealers. The pound's old ERM central rate was 2.95 marks.
The advent of the May 1 UK election, meantime, has sidelined some major players in sterling but has failed to have a serious dent on the pound's trading performance, traders said.

A television debate Sunday between incumbent Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke and Labour's Brown was seen by analysts to show few differences in economic policy between the two. Labour still commands a lead of more than 20 points over the ruling Conservatives in the opinion polls, with the latest Reuters/NOP poll published Monday showing the gap at 21 points.

A fresh wave of EMU optimism washed across Europe, meantime, after the weekend EU finance ministers meeting. This has depressed the mark across the board and helped give sterling/mark a leg higher, analysts said.

German finance minister Theo Waigel increased confidence in EMU going ahead on time after he was quoted as saying of the deficit criterion for EMU "I have never nailed myself to the cross of three percent".
Sources told Reuters today that German March unemployment, due for release early Tuesday, fell by a bigger-than-expected 190,000 during the month.
"The bottom line is that growth is picking up across the board but the U.S. and the UK are much further down the interest rate cycle," said a trader at a Swiss bank here.
